ai.definition: Passwordless identity technology uses passkeys, which are unique cryptographic keys stored on a device or secure credential service to authenticate users without the need for passwords.
ai.howItWorks: Passkeys work by generating and storing cryptographic keys on devices like smartphones. When a user needs to log in, they simply tap their device to verify their identity using the passkey, which is then sent to the server for authentication. This process eliminates the need for memorized passwords and reduces phishing risks.
ai.problemSolved: Passwordless identity addresses the issues of password reuse, weak passwords, and phishing attacks by providing a more secure and user-friendly alternative to traditional passwords.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturers focus on integrating passkey support into hardware devices such as smartphones, laptops, and smartwatches. This involves software development for secure key generation and storage, as well as ensuring compatibility with existing authentication protocols.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes developing the cryptographic algorithms used to generate and verify passkeys, implementing secure storage solutions on devices, and creating APIs for seamless integration with various identity verification systems.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the development of secure key generation and storage technologies, ensuring compatibility across different platforms, and providing user education on how to use passkeys effectively. Security measures are a significant cost factor due to the need for robust encryption standards.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is expected to grow as more devices support passkeys and organizations adopt them to enhance security measures against phishing attacks and password-related vulnerabilities.
ai.regulation: Regulations vary by region, but there are ongoing efforts to standardize passkey protocols. For instance, the FIDO Alliance has developed standards for passkeys that can be adopted globally.
ai.risks: Risks include potential vulnerabilities in key storage mechanisms, phishing attacks targeting passkeys, and compatibility issues between different devices and services.
ai.profitability: Profitability is driven by adoption rates among businesses and consumers. As more organizations implement passwordless identity solutions, the market for related hardware and software could grow significantly.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving interoperability, expanding support to more devices, and enhancing user experience through seamless integration with existing authentication systems.

glossary.def: A unique cryptographic key used for authenticating users without the need for passwords.

An attack where fraudulent communications are made with the intent of acquiring sensitive information such as usernames, passwords, and credit card details by masquerading as a trustworthy entity in an electronic communication.

subsystems.name: Authenticator
subsystems.role: Generates and stores the private key and verifies the user with a biometric or PIN.

subsystems.name: Client platform
subsystems.role: Mediates between the web page or app and the authenticator through a standard API.
parts: WebAuthn API in browser or OS

subsystems.name: Relying party server
subsystems.role: Registers public keys and verifies signatures to authenticate the user.

subsystems.name: Passkey sync service
subsystems.role: Optionally syncs passkeys across a user's devices so they are not lost.

subsystems.name: Recovery and fallback
subsystems.role: Lets a user regain access if all authenticators are lost or unavailable.

subsystems.name: Enterprise integration
subsystems.role: Connects passwordless login to existing identity systems for workforces.

buildSteps.title: Adopt the standards
buildSteps.detail: Choose FIDO2 and WebAuthn so that any compliant authenticator works; the server stores only public keys.

buildSteps.title: Build registration
buildSteps.detail: On sign-up, the server sends a random challenge; the client calls navigator.credentials.create(); the authenticator creates a key pair, verifies the user, and returns the public key and credential ID.

buildSteps.title: Build authentication
buildSteps.detail: On login, the server sends a challenge; the client calls navigator.credentials.get(); the authenticator signs the challenge; the server verifies the signature against the stored public key.

buildSteps.title: Design the user experience
buildSteps.detail: Prompt for Touch ID, Windows Hello, or Android biometrics, and support cross-device sign-in by showing a QR code that a phone scans.

buildSteps.title: Implement account recovery
buildSteps.detail: Offer backup authenticators, one-time recovery codes, and a manual identity-proofing process for lost devices.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with enterprise identity
buildSteps.detail: Connect to OIDC or SAML providers and enforce conditional access policies based on device compliance.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and migrate
buildSteps.detail: Roll out gradually, allow password fallback during the transition, then remove passwords once adoption is high.

prerequisites.why: the foundation: a private key never leaves the device and a matching public key is stored on the server.
define the API and protocol so authenticators and servers interoperate.
protects private keys from malware and extraction.
provide convenient user verification on phones and laptops.
allows passkeys to be available across a user's devices without manual copying.

pathway.milestone: Passkeys supported by major platforms and browsers, with early adoption in consumer apps and some enterprises.
pathway.unlocks: users can sign in without passwords on a growing number of services.

pathway.milestone: Passwordless becomes the default for new accounts and enterprise SSO integrates passkeys.
pathway.unlocks: reduced phishing and credential-stuffing attacks at scale.

pathway.milestone: Emerging standards for cross-platform passkey portability.
pathway.unlocks: users can move passkeys between ecosystems without losing access.

pathway.milestone: Integration with verifiable credentials and decentralized identity.
pathway.unlocks: passwordless identity for government, finance, and cross-border services.
